title.zh: 卷二百五十八 列傳第十七 曹彬 潘美 李超
title.en: Volume 258 Biographies 17: Cao Bin, Pan Mei, Li Chao
title.raw: 卷二百五十八 列傳第十七 曹彬 潘美 李超 Volume 258 Biographies 17: Cao Bin, Pan Mei, Li Chao

sentences.zh: 曹彬，字國華，真定靈壽人。

translations.literal: Cao Bin, styled Guohua, was a man of Lingshou in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bin, styled Guohua, was a native of Lingshou in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父芸，成德軍節度都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: His father Yun was the military commander-in-chief of the Chengde Army under the military governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun served as overall military commander of the Chengde Army under its military governor.

sentences.zh: 彬始生周歲，父母以百玩之具羅于席，觀其所取。

translations.literal: When Bin had just reached one year of age, his parents spread a hundred playthings on a mat to see what he would take.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin was one year old, his parents laid out a hundred toys on a mat to see which he would choose.

sentences.zh: 彬左手持干戈，右手持俎豆，斯須取一印，他無所視，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Bin took weapons in his left hand and ritual vessels in his right; in a moment he chose a seal and looked at nothing else — all were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Bin grasped weapons in his left hand and ritual vessels in his right; in a moment he picked up a seal and paid no attention to anything else, and everyone marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 及長，氣質淳厚。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his temperament was simple and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, his character was plain and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，為成德軍牙將。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era of Han, he served as a junior officer in the Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou reign of the Later Han, he served as a junior officer in the Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 節帥武行德見其端懿，指謂左右曰：「此遠大器，非常流也。

translations.literal: The military governor Wu Xingde saw his upright bearing and, pointing him out to those beside him, said: "This one is a vessel for great things — no ordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: The military governor Wu Xingde saw his dignified bearing and, pointing him out to his attendants, said, "This boy is destined for great things — he is no ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」周太祖貴妃張氏，彬從母也。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Zhang of Emperor Taizu of Zhou was Bin's maternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Zhang, consort of the Zhou founder, was Bin's maternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 周祖受禪，召彬歸京師。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder received the abdication, he summoned Bin to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder took the throne, he summoned Bin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 隸世宗帳下，從鎮澶淵，補供奉官，擢河中都監。

translations.literal: He was assigned to Emperor Shizong's staff, followed him to garrison Chanzhou, was appointed a palace attendant, and was promoted to director of the Zhongdu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Emperor Shizong's personal staff, followed him to garrison Chanzhou, was appointed a palace attendant, and was promoted to director of the Zhongdu garrison.

sentences.zh: 蒲帥王仁鎬以彬帝戚，尤加禮遇。

translations.literal: The military governor of Pu, Wang Renhou, because Bin was imperial kin, treated him with particular courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renhou, military governor of Pu, treated Bin with special courtesy because he was related to the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 彬執禮益恭，公府讌集，端簡終日，未嘗旁視。

translations.literal: Bin observed ritual with even greater deference; at gatherings in the official residence he remained upright and restrained all day, never looking aside.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was even more deferential in his conduct; at banquets in the governor's residence he sat upright and restrained all day long, never glancing to either side.

sentences.zh: 仁鎬謂從事曰：「老夫自謂夙夜匪懈，及見監軍矜嚴，始覺己之散率也。」

translations.literal: Renhou said to his staff: "I thought myself diligent day and night, but seeing the supervisory commissioner so stern and disciplined, I realize how lax I have been."
translations.idiomatic: Renhou said to his staff, "I thought myself diligent day and night, but after seeing the supervisory commissioner so stern and disciplined, I realize how lax I have been."

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，改潼關監軍，遷西上閣門使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to supervisory commissioner at Tong Pass and promoted to Upper West Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was made supervisory commissioner at Tong Pass and promoted to Upper West Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，使吳越，致命訖即還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was sent as envoy to Wuyue; when his mission was complete he returned at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was dispatched as envoy to Wuyue and returned immediately after delivering his charge.

sentences.zh: 私覿之禮，一無所受。

translations.literal: He accepted none of the private audience gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of the private gifts offered on the side.

sentences.zh: 吳越人以輕舟追遺之，至於數四，彬猶不受。

translations.literal: The people of Wuyue pursued him in light boats to press gifts on him again and again, yet Bin still refused.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wuyue chased after him in light boats to press gifts on him, doing so again and again, yet Bin still refused.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「吾終拒之，是近名也。

translations.literal: Then he said: "If I keep refusing to the end, that would be courting a reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "If I keep refusing forever, that would be courting a reputation for virtue."

sentences.zh: 」遂受而籍之以歸，悉上送官。

translations.literal: So he accepted them, recorded them, and brought them back, and presented them all to the court.
translations.idiomatic: So he accepted them, recorded them, and brought them back, then presented them all to the court.

sentences.zh: 世宗強還之，彬始拜賜，悉以分遺親舊而不留一錢。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong forced them back on him; Bin then bowed to receive the gift and distributed it entirely among relatives and friends, keeping not a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong insisted on returning them to him; Bin then bowed to accept the gift and distributed it all among relatives and friends, keeping not a single coin.

sentences.zh: 出為晉州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as overall military commissioner of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 一日，與主帥暨賓從環坐於野，會鄰道守將走價馳書來詣，使者素不識彬，潛問人曰：「孰為曹監軍？

translations.literal: One day he sat in a circle with the commanding general and his entourage in the open country when a neighboring circuit's defending general sent a messenger racing with a letter; the envoy did not know Bin and quietly asked: "Which one is Supervisory Commissioner Cao?"
translations.idiomatic: One day he sat in a circle in the open country with the commanding general and his attendants when a neighboring circuit's defending general sent a messenger racing with a letter; the envoy did not know Bin and quietly asked someone, "Which one is Supervisory Commissioner Cao?"

sentences.zh: 」有指彬以示之，使人以為紿己，笑曰：「豈有國戚近臣，而衣弋綈袍、坐素胡床者乎？

translations.literal: Someone pointed Bin out; the messenger thought he was being fooled and laughed: "How could an imperial kinsman and close courtier wear a plain hemp robe and sit on an unadorned folding stool?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone pointed Bin out to him; the messenger thought he was being deceived and laughed, "How could an imperial kinsman and close courtier wear a plain hemp robe and sit on an unadorned folding stool?"

sentences.zh: 」審視之方信。

translations.literal: Only after looking closely did he believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Only after looking closely did he believe it.

sentences.zh: 遷引進使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖典禁旅，彬中立不倚，非公事未嘗造門，群居讌會，亦所罕預，由是器重焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizu commanded the palace guard, Bin stood neutral and did not lean either way; except on public business he never visited anyone's door, and he rarely joined group banquets — for this Taizu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taizu commanded the palace guard, Bin held himself aloof and impartial; except on official business he never visited anyone's door, and he seldom took part in group banquets — for this Taizu came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，自平陽召歸，謂曰：「我疇昔常欲親汝，汝何故疏我？

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, summoned back from Pingyang, Taizu said to him: "Long ago I often wished to be close to you — why did you keep your distance from me?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, summoned back from Pingyang, the emperor said to him, "Long ago I often wanted to be close to you — why did you keep your distance from me?"

sentences.zh: 」彬頓首謝曰：「臣為周室近親，復忝內職，靖恭守位，猶恐獲過，安敢妄有交結？

translations.literal: Bin prostrated himself and replied: "Your servant is a close kinsman of the Zhou house and also holds an inner-court post; I maintained respectful vigilance in my office, fearing even the least fault — how could I dare form improper connections?"
translations.idiomatic: Bin prostrated himself and replied, "Your servant is a close kinsman of the Zhou house and also holds an inner-court post; I kept my place with respectful vigilance, fearing even the slightest fault — how could I dare form improper connections?"

sentences.zh: 」遷客省使，與王全斌、郭進領騎兵攻河東平樂縣，降其將王超、侯霸榮等千八百人，俘獲千餘人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Receptions; with Wang Quanbin and Guo Jin he led cavalry to attack Pingle County in Hedong, accepting the surrender of generals Wang Chao, Hou Barong, and more than eighteen hundred others, and capturing over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Receptions; with Wang Quanbin and Guo Jin he led cavalry to attack Pingle County in Hedong, accepting the surrender of generals Wang Chao, Hou Barong, and more than eighteen hundred others and capturing over a thousand more.

sentences.zh: 既而賊將蔚進率兵來援，三戰皆敗之。

translations.literal: Then the rebel general Wei Jin came with reinforcements; they defeated him three times.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rebel general Wei Jin came with reinforcements, and they defeated him in three engagements.

sentences.zh: 遂建平樂為平晉軍。

translations.literal: They then established Pingle as the Pingjin Army.
translations.idiomatic: They then established Pingle as the Pingjin Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，改左神武將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he was made General of the Left Divine Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qiande, he was made General of the Left Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 時初克遼州，河東召契丹兵六萬騎來攻平晉，彬與李繼勳等大敗之於城下。

translations.literal: When Liaozhou had just been taken, Hedong summoned sixty thousand Khitan cavalry to attack Pingjin; Bin and Li Jixun and others routed them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaozhou had just been taken, Hedong summoned sixty thousand Khitan cavalry to attack Pingjin; Bin, Li Jixun, and the others routed them below the city walls.

sentences.zh: 俄兼樞密承旨。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was concurrently Grand Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also appointed Grand Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，伐蜀，詔以劉光毅為歸州行營前軍副部署，彬為都監。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year, when an expedition against Shu was ordered, Liu Guangyi was appointed Deputy Forward Camp Commander of Guizhou, with Bin as overall supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year, when an expedition against Shu was ordered, Liu Guangyi was appointed deputy forward commander of the Guizhou field camp and Bin was made overall supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 峽中郡縣悉下，諸將咸欲屠城以逞其欲，彬獨申令戢下，所至悅服。

translations.literal: When commanderies and counties in the gorges all fell, the generals wished to sack towns to satisfy their desires; Bin alone issued orders restraining his subordinates, and wherever they went the people submitted willingly.
translations.idiomatic: When the commanderies and counties in the gorges had all fallen, the generals all wanted to sack towns to satisfy their desires; Bin alone issued orders restraining his troops, and wherever they went the people submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 上聞，降詔褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 兩川平，全斌等晝夜宴飲，不恤軍士，部下漁奪無已，蜀人苦之。

translations.literal: After the Two Rivers were pacified, Quanbin and the others feasted day and night and did not care for the soldiers; their subordinates plundered without end, and the people of Shu suffered.
translations.idiomatic: After the Two Rivers were pacified, Quanbin and the others feasted day and night and neglected the soldiers; their subordinates plundered without end, and the people of Shu suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 彬屢請旋師，全斌等不從。

translations.literal: Bin repeatedly asked to withdraw the army; Quanbin and the others would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Bin repeatedly asked to withdraw the army, but Quanbin and the others would not agree.

sentences.zh: 俄而全師雄等構亂，擁眾十萬，彬復與光毅破之於新繁，卒平蜀亂。

translations.literal: Soon Quan Shi and others stirred rebellion, gathering a host of a hundred thousand; Bin again with Guangyi defeated them at Xinfan and finally quelled the Shu disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Quan Shixiong and others stirred up rebellion and gathered a force of a hundred thousand; Bin again defeated them with Guangyi at Xinfan and finally put down the Shu rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時諸將多取子女玉帛，彬橐中唯圖書、衣衾而已。

translations.literal: At that time most generals took women, jade, and silk; in Bin's pack there were only books and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most of the generals took women, jade, and silk; in Bin's pack there were only books and bedding.

sentences.zh: 及還，上盡得其狀，以全斌等屬吏。

translations.literal: When they returned, the emperor learned the full situation and turned Quanbin and the others over to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, the emperor learned the full situation and turned Quanbin and the others over to the judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 謂彬清介廉謹，授宣徽南院使、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: Declaring Bin upright, incorruptible, and prudent, he appointed him Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Declaring Bin upright, incorruptible, and prudent, the emperor appointed him Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 彬入見，辭曰：「征西將士俱得罪，臣獨受賞，恐無以示勸。

translations.literal: When Bin entered audience he declined, saying: "The western-expedition officers have all been punished; if your servant alone receives reward, I fear there will be no example for encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: When Bin came to audience he declined, saying, "The officers of the western expedition have all been punished; if your servant alone receives reward, I fear there will be no example to encourage others."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿有茂功，又不矜伐，設有微累，仁贍等豈惜言哉？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have great merit and do not boast of it; even if there were a minor flaw, would Renzan and the others spare words?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have great merit and do not boast of it; even if there were some minor fault, would Renzan and the others spare words?"

sentences.zh: 懲勸國之常典，可無讓。」

translations.literal: Punishment and reward are the normal way of the state — you need not demur."
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and reward are the normal way of the state — you need not demur."

sentences.zh: 六年，遣李繼勳、党進率師征太原，命為前軍都監，戰洞渦河，斬二千餘級，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Li Jixun and Dang Jin were sent to lead troops against Taiyuan; Bin was appointed forward-army supervisory commissioner; at the Dongtuo River they beheaded more than two thousand and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Li Jixun and Dang Jin were sent to lead troops against Taiyuan; Bin was appointed forward-army supervisory commissioner; at the Dongtuo River they beheaded more than two thousand and captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，議親征太原，復命為前軍都監，率兵先往，次團柏谷，降賊將陳廷山。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, when a personal expedition against Taiyuan was discussed, he was again appointed forward-army supervisory commissioner; he led troops ahead and halted at Tuanbai Valley, accepting the surrender of the rebel general Chen Tingshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, when a personal expedition against Taiyuan was discussed, he was again appointed forward-army supervisory commissioner; he led troops ahead, halted at Tuanbai Valley, and accepted the surrender of the rebel general Chen Tingshan.

sentences.zh: 又戰城南，薄於濠橋，奪馬千餘。

translations.literal: They fought again south of the city, pressed up to the moat bridge, and seized more than a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again south of the city, pressed up to the moat bridge, and seized more than a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 及太祖至，則已分砦四面，而自主其北。

translations.literal: When Taizu arrived, camps had already been laid out on four sides, and Bin himself held the north.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu arrived, camps had already been laid out on four sides, and Bin himself held the northern position.

sentences.zh: 六年，進檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor with the usual honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 七年，將伐江南。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they were about to campaign against Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they prepared to campaign against Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 九月，彬奉詔與李漢瓊、田欽祚先赴荊南發戰艦，潘美帥步兵繼進。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Bin received orders with Li Hanqiong and Tian Qinzuo to go first to Jingnan to launch warships; Pan Mei led infantry following after.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bin received orders with Li Hanqiong and Tian Qinzuo to go first to Jingnan to launch the warships, while Pan Mei led the infantry in support.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔以彬為升州西南路行營馬步軍戰棹都部署，分兵由荊南順流而東，破峽口砦，進克池州，連克當塗、蕪湖二縣，駐軍採石磯。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict made Bin Overall Forward Commander of cavalry, infantry, and war vessels for the southwest route to Shengzhou; forces divided and went east from Jingnan downstream, took the Xikou fort, then captured Chizhou, and in succession took Dangtu and Wuhu, encamping at Caishiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict appointed Bin overall commander of cavalry, infantry, and war vessels for the southwest route to Shengzhou; dividing his forces, he went east from Jingnan downstream, took the Xikou fort, captured Chizhou, then in succession took Dangtu and Wuhu, and encamped at Caishiji.

sentences.zh: 十一月，作浮梁，跨大江以濟師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they built a floating bridge across the great river to ferry the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they built a floating bridge across the great river to ferry the army across.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大破其軍於白鷺洲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they routed the enemy army at Bailuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they routed the enemy army at Bailuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，又破其軍于新林港。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year they again defeated the enemy at Xinlingang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year they again defeated the enemy army at Xinlingang.

sentences.zh: 二月，師進次秦淮，江南水陸十餘萬陳於城下，大敗之，俘斬數萬計。

translations.literal: In the second month the army advanced to the Qinhuai; more than a hundred thousand Jiangnan land and river forces were drawn up below the city; they were crushingly defeated, with tens of thousands captured or slain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the army advanced to the Qinhuai; more than a hundred thousand Jiangnan land and river forces were drawn up below the city, and they were crushingly defeated, with tens of thousands captured or slain.

sentences.zh: 及浮梁成，吳人出兵來禦，破之於白鷺洲。

translations.literal: When the floating bridge was finished, Wu forces came out to resist; they were defeated again at Bailuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the floating bridge was finished, Wu forces came out to resist, and they were defeated again at Bailuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自三月至八月，連破之，進克潤州。

translations.literal: From the third month to the eighth month they kept winning and took Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From the third month to the eighth month they kept defeating the enemy and advanced to capture Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 金陵受圍，至是凡三時，吳人樵采路絕，頻經敗衄，李煜危急，遣其臣徐鉉奉表詣闕，乞緩師，上不之省。

translations.literal: Jinling had been besieged for three seasons by then; the Wu people's firewood and forage routes were cut off, they suffered defeat after defeat, Li Yu was in desperate straits, and sent his minister Xu Xuan with a memorial to court begging a respite — the emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling had been under siege for three seasons by then; the Wu people's routes for firewood and foraging were cut off, they suffered defeat after defeat, Li Yu was in desperate straits, and he sent his minister Xu Xuan with a memorial to court begging a respite — the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 先是，大軍列三砦，美居守北偏，圖其形勢來上。

translations.literal: Earlier the main army had set three camps; Mei held the northern flank and sent up a map of the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the main army had set up three camps; Mei held the northern flank and sent up a map of the terrain.

sentences.zh: 太祖指北砦謂使者曰：「吳人必夜出兵來寇，爾亟去，令曹彬速成深溝以自固，無墮其計中。

translations.literal: Taizu pointed at the northern camp and told the envoy: "The Wu will surely send troops by night to raid; go back quickly and tell Cao Bin to finish deep ditches at once for defense — do not fall into their trap."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu pointed at the northern camp and told the envoy, "The Wu will surely send troops by night to raid; go back quickly and tell Cao Bin to finish deep ditches at once for defense — do not fall into their trap."

sentences.zh: 」既成，吳兵果夜來襲，美率所部依新溝拒之，吳人大敗。

translations.literal: When it was done, Wu troops did come by night; Mei led his troops and relying on the new ditch repulsed them — the Wu were heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done, Wu troops did come by night; Mei led his troops and, relying on the new ditch, repulsed them, and the Wu were heavily defeated.

sentences.zh: 奏至，上笑曰：「果如此。」

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor laughed: "It turned out exactly so."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor laughed and said, "It turned out exactly so."

sentences.zh: 長圍中，彬每緩師，冀煜歸服。

translations.literal: During the long siege Bin repeatedly slowed operations, hoping Li Yu would submit.
translations.idiomatic: During the long siege Bin repeatedly slowed operations, hoping Li Yu would submit of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 十一月，彬又使人諭之曰：「事勢如此，所惜者一城生聚，若能歸命，策之上也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Bin again sent someone to instruct him: "The situation being what it is, what is at stake is the lives of everyone in one city; if you can surrender, that is the best course."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Bin again sent someone to instruct him, "The situation being what it is, what is at stake is the lives of everyone in one city; if you can surrender, that is the best course."

sentences.zh: 」城垂克，彬忽稱疾不視事，諸將皆來問疾。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, Bin suddenly claimed illness and would not attend to affairs; all the generals came to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, Bin suddenly claimed illness and would not attend to affairs; all the generals came to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「余之疾非藥石所能愈，惟須諸公誠心自誓，以克城之日，不妄殺一人，則自愈矣。

translations.literal: Bin said: "My illness is not something medicine can cure — only if you gentlemen swear sincerely that on the day the city is taken you will not kill a person wantonly will I recover."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "My illness is not something medicine can cure — only if you gentlemen swear sincerely that on the day the city is taken you will not kill anyone wantonly will I recover."

sentences.zh: 」諸將許諾，共焚香為誓。

translations.literal: The generals promised and together burned incense to swear.
translations.idiomatic: The generals promised and together burned incense to swear an oath.

sentences.zh: 明日，稍愈。

translations.literal: The next day he was somewhat better.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was somewhat better.

sentences.zh: 又明日，城陷。

translations.literal: The day after that the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The day after that the city fell.

sentences.zh: 煜與其臣百餘人詣軍門請罪，彬慰安之，待以賓禮，請煜入宮治裝，彬以數騎待宮門外。

translations.literal: Li Yu with more than a hundred ministers came to the camp gate to ask punishment; Bin comforted them and received them with guest ritual, asking Li Yu to enter the palace to pack; Bin waited with a few horsemen outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu came with more than a hundred ministers to the camp gate to ask punishment; Bin comforted them and received them with the courtesy due guests, asked Li Yu to enter the palace to pack his belongings, and waited with a few horsemen outside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 左右密謂彬曰：「煜入或不測，奈何？

translations.literal: Those beside him whispered to Bin: "If Li Yu enters, there may be unforeseen danger — what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him whispered to Bin, "If Li Yu enters the palace, there may be unforeseen danger — what then?"

sentences.zh: 」彬笑曰：「煜素愞無斷，既已降，必不能自引決。

translations.literal: Bin smiled: "Li Yu has always been weak and indecisive; having already surrendered, he surely cannot bring himself to take his own life."
translations.idiomatic: Bin smiled and said, "Li Yu has always been weak and indecisive; having already surrendered, he surely cannot bring himself to take his own life."

sentences.zh: 」煜之君臣，卒賴保全。

translations.literal: Li Yu and his ministers were finally preserved thanks to this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu and his ministers were finally preserved thanks to this.

sentences.zh: 自出師至凱旋，士眾畏服，無輕肆者。

translations.literal: From the expedition's start to triumphant return, the soldiers feared and respected him — none were insolent.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of the expedition to triumphant return, the soldiers feared and respected him, and none were insolent.

sentences.zh: 及入見，刺稱「奉敕江南幹事回」，其謙恭不伐如此。

translations.literal: When he entered audience he briefly styled himself "returned from conducting affairs in Jiangnan on imperial order" — such was his humility and refusal to boast.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered audience he briefly styled himself "returned from conducting affairs in Jiangnan on imperial order" — such was his humility and refusal to boast.

sentences.zh: 初，彬之總師也，太祖謂曰：「俟克李煜，當以卿為使相。

translations.literal: When Bin first took overall command, Taizu told him: "When Li Yu is taken, I shall make you a commissioner-grandee."
translations.idiomatic: When Bin first took overall command, Taizu told him, "When Li Yu is taken, I shall make you a commissioner-grandee."

sentences.zh: 」副帥潘美預以為賀。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Pan Mei prepared congratulations in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Pan Mei prepared congratulations in advance.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「不然，夫是行也，仗天威，遵廟謨，乃能成事，吾何功哉，況使相極品乎！

translations.literal: Bin said: "Not so. This campaign relied on Heaven's majesty and followed the temple plan — only thus could it succeed; what merit have I? And the highest rank of commissioner-grandee besides!"
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Not so. This campaign relied on Heaven's majesty and followed the plan laid down in the ancestral temple — only thus could it succeed; what merit have I? And the highest rank of commissioner-grandee besides!"

sentences.zh: 」美曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: Mei said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」彬曰：「太原未平爾。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Taiyuan has not yet been pacified, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Taiyuan has not yet been pacified, that's all."

sentences.zh: 」及還，獻俘。

translations.literal: When they returned they presented captives.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned they presented the captives.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「本授卿使相，然劉繼元未下，姑少待之。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "I was going to appoint you commissioner-grandee, but since Liu Jiyuan has not yet fallen, wait a little."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "I was going to appoint you commissioner-grandee, but since Liu Jiyuan has not yet fallen, wait a little."

sentences.zh: 」既聞此語，美竊視彬微笑。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Mei stole a glance at Bin and smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Mei stole a glance at Bin and smiled.

sentences.zh: 上覺，遽詰所以，美不敢隱，遂以實對。

translations.literal: The emperor noticed, immediately questioned why; Mei dared not hide it and answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed, immediately questioned why, and Mei dared not hide it and answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 上亦大笑，乃賜彬錢二十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor also laughed greatly and then granted Bin two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also laughed heartily and then granted Bin two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 彬退曰：「人生何必使相，好官亦不過多得錢爾。

translations.literal: Bin withdrew saying: "What need is there in life for commissioner-grandee rank? A good office is nothing but getting more money, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Bin withdrew saying, "What need is there in life for commissioner-grandee rank? A good office is nothing but getting more money, that's all."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，拜樞密使、檢校太尉、忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Bureau Chief, Honorary Grand Commandant, and military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Bureau Chief, Honorary Grand Commandant, and military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，詔彬將幽州行營前軍馬步水陸之師，與潘美等北伐，分路進討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi an edict ordered Bin to command the forward army's cavalry, infantry, and river-sea forces of the Youzhou field camp; with Pan Mei and others he marched north, advancing by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi an edict ordered Bin to command the forward army's cavalry, infantry, and river-sea forces of the Youzhou field camp; with Pan Mei and others he marched north, advancing by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 三月，敗契丹于固安，破涿州，戎人來援，大破之于城南。

translations.literal: In the third month they defeated the Khitans at Gu'an, took Zhuozhou; when barbarian reinforcements came they heavily defeated them south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they defeated the Khitans at Gu'an and took Zhuozhou; when barbarian reinforcements came they heavily defeated them south of the city.

sentences.zh: 四月，又與米信破契丹於新城，斬首二百級。

translations.literal: In the fourth month with Mi Xin they again defeated the Khitans at Xincheng, beheading two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, together with Mi Xin, they again defeated the Khitans at Xincheng and beheaded two hundred.

sentences.zh: 五月，戰于岐溝關，諸軍敗績，退屯易州，臨易水而營。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they fought at Qigou Pass; the armies suffered defeat and withdrew to camp at Yizhou on the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they fought at Qigou Pass; the armies suffered defeat and withdrew to encamp at Yizhou on the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 上聞，亟令分屯邊城，追諸將歸闕。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he urgently ordered them to garrison the border towns separately and recalled the generals to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he urgently ordered them to garrison the border towns separately and recalled the generals to court.

sentences.zh: 先是，賀令圖等言於上曰：「契丹主少，母后專政，寵倖用事，請乘其釁，以取幽薊。

translations.literal: Earlier He Lingtu and others had told the emperor: "The Khitan ruler is young; the empress dowager holds power and favorites govern — please seize this opening to take You and Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier He Lingtu and others had told the emperor, "The Khitan ruler is young; the empress dowager holds power and favorites govern affairs — please seize this opening to take You and Ji."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣彬與崔彥進、米信自雄州，田重進趣飛狐，潘美出雁門，約期齊舉。

translations.literal: Bin was then sent with Cui Yanjin and Mi Xin from Xiongzhou, Tian Chongjin toward Feihu, Pan Mei out from Yanmen — with a fixed date to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was then sent with Cui Yanjin and Mi Xin from Xiongzhou, Tian Chongjin toward Feihu, and Pan Mei out from Yanmen, with a fixed date to advance together.

sentences.zh: 將發，上謂之曰：「潘美之師但先趣雲、應，卿等以十萬眾聲言取幽州，且持重緩行，不得貪利。

translations.literal: Before departure the emperor told them: "Pan Mei's force need only press Yun and Ying first; you with a hundred thousand men proclaim that you will take Youzhou and march slowly and with weight — do not grasp after quick profit."
translations.idiomatic: Before departure the emperor told them, "Pan Mei's force need only press Yun and Ying first; you with a hundred thousand men proclaim that you will take Youzhou and march slowly and with weight — do not grasp after quick profit."

sentences.zh: 彼聞大兵至，必悉眾救范陽，不暇援山後矣。

translations.literal: When they hear the great army is coming they will surely muster all forces to save Fanyang and have no time to aid the lands behind the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear the great army is coming they will surely muster all their forces to save Fanyang and have no time to aid the lands behind the mountains.

sentences.zh: 」既而，美之師先下寰、朔、雲、應等州，重進又取飛狐、靈丘、蔚州，多得山後要害地，彬亦連下州縣，勢大振。

translations.literal: Afterward Mei's troops first took Huan, Shuo, Yun, Ying, and other prefectures; Chongjin also took Feihu, Lingqiu, and Weizhou, securing many key positions behind the mountains; Bin also took prefectures and counties in succession and their momentum greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Mei's troops first took Huan, Shuo, Yun, Ying, and other prefectures; Chongjin also took Feihu, Lingqiu, and Weizhou, securing many key positions behind the mountains; Bin also took prefectures and counties in succession, and their momentum greatly rose.

sentences.zh: 每奏至，上已訝彬進軍之速。

translations.literal: Each time a memorial arrived, the emperor was already surprised at how quickly Bin was advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a memorial arrived, the emperor was already surprised at how quickly Bin was advancing.

sentences.zh: 及彬次涿州，旬日食盡，因退師雄州以援餉饋。

translations.literal: When Bin halted at Zhuozhou, their provisions were exhausted within ten days, so he withdrew the army to Xiongzhou to secure supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin halted at Zhuozhou, their provisions were exhausted within ten days, so he withdrew the army to Xiongzhou to secure supplies.

sentences.zh: 上聞之曰：「豈有敵人在前，反退軍以援芻粟，失策之甚也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he said: "How can there be an enemy in front and yet the army withdraws to fetch fodder and grain — this is a grave error in strategy."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he said, "How can there be an enemy in front and yet the army withdraws to fetch fodder and grain — this is a grave error in strategy."

sentences.zh: 」亟遣使止彬勿前，急引師緣白溝河與米信軍會，案兵養銳，以張西師之勢；

translations.literal: He urgently sent envoys to stop Bin from advancing further and ordered him to lead his troops quickly along the Baigou River to join Mi Xin's army, hold his forces and restore their edge, and thereby display the strength of the western army.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently sent envoys to stop Bin from advancing further and ordered him to lead his troops quickly along the Baigou River to join Mi Xin's army, hold his forces and restore their edge, and thereby display the strength of the western army.

sentences.zh: 俟美等盡略山後地，會重進之師而東，合勢以取幽州。

translations.literal: He was to wait until Mei and the others had fully overrun the lands behind the mountains, then join Chongjin's army and march east, combining their strength to take Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was to wait until Mei and the others had fully overrun the lands behind the mountains, then join Chongjin's army and march east, combining their strength to take Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 時彬部下諸將，聞美及重進累建功，而已握重兵不能有所攻取，謀議蜂起。

translations.literal: At that time Bin's subordinate generals, hearing that Mei and Chongjin had repeatedly won merit while they themselves held heavy forces yet could achieve no capture, raised plans and objections in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bin's subordinate generals, hearing that Mei and Chongjin had repeatedly won merit while they themselves held heavy forces yet could achieve no capture, raised plans and objections in swarms.

sentences.zh: 彬不得已，乃復裹糧再往攻涿州。

translations.literal: Bin, having no choice, again packed provisions and went once more to attack Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, having no choice, again packed provisions and went once more to attack Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹大眾當前，時方炎暑，軍士乏困，糧且盡，彬退軍，無復行伍，遂為所躡而敗。

translations.literal: A great Khitan host stood before them; it was the height of summer heat, the soldiers were exhausted, and provisions were nearly gone; Bin withdrew, his army no longer in formation, and was pursued and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A great Khitan host stood before them; it was the height of summer heat, the soldiers were exhausted, and provisions were nearly gone; Bin withdrew, his army no longer in formation, and was pursued and defeated.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，被疾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 上趣駕臨問，手為和藥，仍賜白金萬兩。

translations.literal: The emperor hastened in person to inquire after him, mixed medicine with his own hands, and also granted ten thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hastened in person to inquire after him, mixed medicine with his own hands, and also granted ten thousand taels of white silver.

sentences.zh: 問以後事，對曰：「臣無事可言。

translations.literal: Asked about affairs after his death, he replied: "Your servant has nothing to say."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about affairs after his death, he replied, "Your servant has nothing to say."

sentences.zh: 臣二子材器可取，臣若內舉，皆堪為將。

translations.literal: "Your servant's two sons have ability worth taking; if your servant recommends from within the family, both are fit to be generals."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant's two sons have ability worth taking; if your servant recommends from within the family, both are fit to be generals."

sentences.zh: 」上問其優劣，對曰：「璨不如瑋。

translations.literal: The emperor asked which was superior; he replied: "Can is not the equal of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked which was superior; he replied, "Can is not the equal of Wei."

sentences.zh: 」六月薨，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上臨哭之慟，對輔臣語及彬，必流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to mourn him bitterly; whenever he spoke of Bin to his chief ministers, he would shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him bitterly; whenever he spoke of Bin to his chief ministers, he would shed tears.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，追封濟陽郡王，諡武惠；

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyang, with the posthumous title Wuhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyang, with the posthumous title Wuhui.

sentences.zh: 且贈其妻高氏韓國夫人；

translations.literal: His wife, née Gao, was also granted the title Lady of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Gao, was also granted the title Lady of Han.

sentences.zh: 官其親族、門客、親校十餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten of his kinsmen, retainers, and personal guards were given official posts.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of his kinsmen, retainers, and personal guards were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔彬與趙普配饗太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered Bin and Zhao Pu to share sacrificial honors in the court of Taizu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ordered Bin and Zhao Pu to share sacrificial honors in the court of Taizu's temple.

sentences.zh: 彬性仁敬和厚，在朝廷未嘗忤旨，亦未嘗言人過失。

translations.literal: Bin's nature was benevolent, respectful, harmonious, and sincere; at court he never defied the imperial will, nor did he ever speak of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's nature was benevolent, respectful, harmonious, and sincere; at court he never defied the imperial will, nor did he ever speak of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 伐二國，秋毫無所取。

translations.literal: In campaigns against two states he took not the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns against two states he took not the slightest thing.

sentences.zh: 位兼將相，不以等威自異。

translations.literal: Though his rank combined general and minister, he did not set himself apart by rank and dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank combined general and minister, he did not set himself apart by rank and dignity.

sentences.zh: 遇士夫於途，必引車避之。

translations.literal: When he met scholars on the road he always pulled his carriage aside to yield.
translations.idiomatic: When he met scholars on the road he always pulled his carriage aside to yield.

sentences.zh: 不名下吏，每白事，必冠而後見。

translations.literal: He did not summon subordinates by name; whenever they reported business he always put on his cap before receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: He did not summon subordinates by name; whenever they reported business he always put on his cap before receiving them.

sentences.zh: 居官奉入給宗族，無餘積。

translations.literal: His official salary went to support his clan, and he kept no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: His official salary went to support his clan, and he kept no surplus.

sentences.zh: 平蜀回，太祖從容問官吏善否，對曰：「軍政之外，非臣所聞也。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Shu, Taizu casually asked whether the officials were good or bad; he replied: "Apart from military affairs, that is not something your servant has heard of."
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shu, Taizu casually asked whether the officials were good or bad; he replied, "Apart from military affairs, that is not something your servant has heard of."

sentences.zh: 」固問之，唯薦隨軍轉運使沈倫廉謹可任。

translations.literal: Pressed further, he recommended only the army transport commissioner Shen Lun as upright and prudent and fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed further, he recommended only the army transport commissioner Shen Lun as upright and prudent and fit for office.

sentences.zh: 為帥知徐州日，有吏犯罪，既具案，逾年而後杖之，人莫知其故。

translations.literal: When he was commander and prefect of Xuzhou, a clerk committed a crime; after the case was complete, more than a year passed before he was flogged, and no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: When he was commander and prefect of Xuzhou, a clerk committed a crime; after the case was complete, more than a year passed before he was flogged, and no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「吾聞此人新娶婦，若杖之，其舅姑必以婦為不利，而朝夕笞詈之，使不能自存。

translations.literal: Bin said: "I heard this man had just married; if he were flogged, his parents-in-law would surely blame the wife for misfortune and beat and revile her day and night until she could not survive."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "I heard this man had just married; if he were flogged, his parents-in-law would surely blame the wife for misfortune and beat and revile her day and night until she could not survive."

sentences.zh: 吾故緩其事，然法亦未嘗屈焉。

translations.literal: "I therefore delayed the matter, yet the law was never bent."
translations.idiomatic: "I therefore delayed the matter, yet the law was never bent."

sentences.zh: 」北征之失律也，趙昌言表請行軍法。

translations.literal: When Bin violated military discipline on the northern expedition, Zhao Changyan submitted a memorial requesting that military law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin violated military discipline on the northern expedition, Zhao Changyan submitted a memorial requesting that military law be applied.

sentences.zh: 及昌言自延安還，被劾，不得入見。

translations.literal: When Changyan returned from Yan'an he was impeached and not permitted to enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Changyan returned from Yan'an he was impeached and not permitted to enter audience.

sentences.zh: 彬在右府，為請於上，乃許朝謁。

translations.literal: Bin, in the Bureau of Military Affairs, pleaded for him before the emperor, and audience was then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, in the Bureau of Military Affairs, pleaded for him before the emperor, and audience was then permitted.

sentences.zh: 子璨、珝、瑋、玹、玘、珣、琮。

translations.literal: His sons were Can, Xu, Wei, Xuan, Qi, Xun, and Cong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Can, Xu, Wei, Xuan, Qi, Xun, and Cong.

sentences.zh: 珝娶秦王女興平郡主，至昭宣使。

translations.literal: Xu married the Princess of Xingping, daughter of the Prince of Qin, and rose to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu married the Princess of Xingping, daughter of the Prince of Qin, and rose to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玹左藏庫副使，玘尚書虞部員外郎，珣東上閣門使，琮西上閣門副使。

translations.literal: Xuan was Deputy Commissioner of the Left Treasury; Qi was Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works; Xun was Upper East Gate Commissioner; Cong was Deputy Upper West Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was Deputy Commissioner of the Left Treasury; Qi was Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works; Xun was Upper East Gate Commissioner; Cong was Deputy Upper West Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 玘之女，即慈聖光獻皇后也。

translations.literal: Qi's daughter was none other than Empress Cisheng Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's daughter was none other than Empress Cisheng Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 芸，累贈魏王。

translations.literal: Yun was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 彬，韓王。

translations.literal: Bin was Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 玘，吳王，諡曰安僖。

translations.literal: Qi was Prince of Wu, with the posthumous title Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Prince of Wu, with the posthumous title Anxi.

sentences.zh: 玘之子佾、傅。

translations.literal: Qi's sons were Yi and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's sons were Yi and Fu.

sentences.zh: 佾見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Yi is treated in the Biographies of Imperial Affines.
translations.idiomatic: Yi is treated in the Biographies of Imperial Affines.

sentences.zh: 傅，后兄也，榮州刺史，諡恭懷。

translations.literal: Fu, the empress's elder brother, was Prefect of Rongzhou, with the posthumous title Gonghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, the empress's elder brother, was Prefect of Rongzhou, with the posthumous title Gonghuai.

sentences.zh: 子 璨

translations.literal: Son: Can
translations.idiomatic: Son: Can

sentences.zh: 璨，字韜光，性沉毅，善射，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Can, styled Taoguang, was by nature steady and resolute, skilled in archery, and entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Can, styled Taoguang, was by nature steady and resolute, skilled in archery, and entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 常從彬征討，得與計議，彬以為類己，特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: He often followed Bin on campaigns and was allowed to join in planning; Bin thought him like himself and favored him especially.
translations.idiomatic: He often followed Bin on campaigns and was allowed to join in planning; Bin thought him like himself and favored him especially.

sentences.zh: 遷宮苑副使，出為高陽關及鎮、魏、並、代、趙五州都監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Parks and sent out as overall commissioner of Gaoyang Pass and the five prefectures of Zhen, Wei, Bing, Dai, and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Parks and sent out as overall commissioner of Gaoyang Pass and the five prefectures of Zhen, Wei, Bing, Dai, and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，命知定州，改尚食使。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was ordered to govern Dingzhou and was transferred to Commissioner of Imperial Food.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was ordered to govern Dingzhou and was transferred to Commissioner of Imperial Food.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，領富州刺史，徙知代州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was given charge of Fuzhou and was transferred to govern Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was given charge of Fuzhou and was transferred to govern Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢為鎮州行營鈐轄，徙綏、銀、夏、麟、府等州鈐轄。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Controller of the Zhenzhou field camp and transferred to controller of Sui, Yin, Xia, Lin, and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Controller of the Zhenzhou field camp and transferred to controller of Sui, Yin, Xia, Lin, and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，屢戰有功。

translations.literal: When the Khitans invaded he fought repeatedly with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded he fought repeatedly with merit.

sentences.zh: 諸將多欲窮追，璨慮有伏，力止之。

translations.literal: Most generals wished to pursue to the end; Can, fearing an ambush, strongly stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Most generals wished to pursue to the end; Can, fearing an ambush, strongly stopped them.

sentences.zh: 至道初，遷四方館使、知靈州，徙河西鈐轄，改引進使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and governor of Lingzhou, moved to controller of Hexi, and changed to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhidao he was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and governor of Lingzhou, moved to controller of Hexi, and changed to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys.

sentences.zh: 范廷召將兵出塞，命璨為之副。

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao led troops beyond the frontier; Can was appointed his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao led troops beyond the frontier; Can was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，起復，為鄜延路副都部署，拜趙州刺史，領武州團練使，充麟、府、濁輪副部署。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning; he became Deputy Overall Commander of the Fuyan circuit, was appointed Prefect of Zhao, given charge of Wuzhou as regimental commissioner, and made deputy commander of Lin, Fu, and Zhuolun.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning; he became Deputy Overall Commander of the Fuyan circuit, was appointed Prefect of Zhao, given charge of Wuzhou as regimental commissioner, and made deputy commander of Lin, Fu, and Zhuolun.

sentences.zh: 出蕃兵邀繼遷，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: He led barbarian troops to intercept Jiqian and captured and beheaded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: He led barbarian troops to intercept Jiqian and captured and beheaded a great many.

sentences.zh: 入為樞密都承旨，改領亳州團練使。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was transferred to regimental commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was transferred to regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，命為鎮、定、高陽關三路行營都鈐轄，領康州防禦使，再知定州。

translations.literal: When the Khitans invaded he was appointed Overall Controller of the three-route field camp of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, given charge of Kangzhou as defense commissioner, and again made governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded he was appointed Overall Controller of the three-route field camp of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, given charge of Kangzhou as defense commissioner, and again made governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，拜侍衛馬軍副都指揮使、天德軍節度。

translations.literal: The next winter he was appointed Deputy Commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard and military governor of the Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he was appointed Deputy Commander of the Palace Cavalry Guard and military governor of the Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 入為東京舊城都巡檢使，連拜彰國、保靜、武甯、忠武等軍節度使。

translations.literal: He entered court as Overall Inspector of the Old City of the Eastern Capital and in succession was appointed military governor of the Zhangguo, Baojing, Wuning, and Zhongwu armies.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Overall Inspector of the Old City of the Eastern Capital and in succession was appointed military governor of the Zhangguo, Baojing, Wuning, and Zhongwu armies.

sentences.zh: 在禁衛十餘年，未嘗忤旨。

translations.literal: He served in the palace guard for more than ten years and never defied the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the palace guard for more than ten years and never defied the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年春，以足疾授河陽節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Tianxi, because of illness in his feet he was made military governor of Heyang and Concurrent Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Tianxi, because of illness in his feet he was made military governor of Heyang and Concurrent Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十，贈中書令，諡武懿。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy, and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged seventy, and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 璨起貴胄，以孝謹稱，能自奮厲，以世其家。

translations.literal: Can rose from noble birth, was known for filial piety and prudence, and was able to exert himself and carry on the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose from noble birth, was known for filial piety and prudence, and was able to exert himself and carry on the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 習知韜略，好讀《左氏春秋》，善撫士卒，兼著威愛。

translations.literal: He was versed in strategy, loved to read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, was skilled at comforting soldiers, and combined authority with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in strategy, loved to read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, was skilled at comforting soldiers, and combined authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 雖輕財不逮其父，而敬人和厚，亦有父風。

translations.literal: Though he was less indifferent to wealth than his father, he was respectful toward others and generous, and also had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was less indifferent to wealth than his father, he was respectful toward others and generous, and also had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 子儀，官至耀州觀察使。

translations.literal: His son Yi rose to the post of Observation Commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi rose to the post of Observation Commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 子 瑋

translations.literal: Son: Wei
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wei

sentences.zh: 瑋，字寶臣。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Baochen.

sentences.zh: 父彬，曆武甯、天平軍節度使，皆以瑋為牙內都虞候，補西頭供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: His father Bin, while serving successively as military governor of Wuning and Tianping, always made Wei Inner Staff Chief Commandant; he entered office as Western Head Palace Attendant and Gate Usher.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin, while serving successively as military governor of Wuning and Tianping, always made Wei Inner Staff Chief Commandant; he entered office as Western Head Palace Attendant and Gate Usher.

sentences.zh: 沉勇有謀，喜讀書，通《春秋三傳》，于《左氏》尤深。

translations.literal: He was deep, brave, and resourceful, loved to read, mastered the Three Commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and was especially profound in the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep, brave, and resourceful, loved to read, mastered the Three Commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and was especially profound in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷叛，諸將數出無功，太宗問彬：「誰可將者？

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian rebelled the generals went out several times without success; Taizong asked Bin: "Who can command?"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian rebelled the generals went out several times without success; Taizong asked Bin, "Who can command?"

sentences.zh: 」彬曰：「臣少子瑋可任。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Your servant's youngest son Wei is fit for the task."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Your servant's youngest son Wei is fit for the task."

sentences.zh: 」即召見，以本官同知渭州，時年十九。

translations.literal: He was summoned at once and, retaining his original rank, was made co-governor of Weizhou; he was then nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned at once and, retaining his original rank, was made co-governor of Weizhou; he was then nineteen.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改內殿崇班、知渭州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded he was changed to Inner Hall Honored Guard and made governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was changed to Inner Hall Honored Guard and made governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴明有部分，賞罰立決，犯令者無所貸。

translations.literal: He commanded the army with strict clarity and order; rewards and punishments were decided on the spot, and violators were never spared.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the army with strict clarity and order; rewards and punishments were decided on the spot, and violators were never spared.

sentences.zh: 善用間，周知虜動靜，舉措如老將。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using spies, fully knew the enemy's movements, and acted like a veteran general.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in using spies, fully knew the enemy's movements, and acted like a veteran general.

sentences.zh: 彬卒，請持喪，不允，改閣門通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Bin died he asked to observe mourning but was not permitted; he was transferred to Gate Affairs Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin died he asked to observe mourning but was not permitted; he was transferred to Gate Affairs Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閣門副使，徙知鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Upper West Gate Commissioner and transferred to govern Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Deputy Upper West Gate Commissioner and transferred to govern Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷虐用其國人，瑋知其下多怨，即移書諸部，諭以朝廷恩信，撫養無所間，以動諸羌。

translations.literal: Li Jiqian cruelly exploited his own people; Wei knew his subjects were full of resentment and at once sent letters to the various tribes, instructing them in the court's favor and trust and that they would be cared for without discrimination, so as to move the Qiang peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqian cruelly exploited his own people; Wei knew his subjects were full of resentment and at once sent letters to the various tribes, instructing them in the court's favor and trust and that they would be cared for without discrimination, so as to move the Qiang peoples.

sentences.zh: 由是康奴等族請內附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Kangnu and other tribes requested to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Kangnu and other tribes requested to submit inward.

sentences.zh: 繼遷略西蕃還，瑋邀擊于石門川，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: When Jiqian returned from raiding the western barbarians, Wei intercepted him at Shimen River and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian returned from raiding the western barbarians, Wei intercepted him at Shimen River and captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 以鎮戎軍據平地，便於騎戰，非中國之利，請自隴山以東，循古長城塹以為限。

translations.literal: Because Zhenrong Army stood on level ground favorable to cavalry combat and not to China's advantage, he requested that from east of Longshan the ancient Great Wall trench be followed as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhenrong Army stood on level ground favorable to cavalry combat and not to China's advantage, he requested that from east of Longshan the ancient Great Wall trench be followed as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 又以弓箭手皆土人，習障塞蹊隧，曉羌語，耐塞苦，官未嘗與兵械資糧，而每戰輒使先拒賊，恐無以責死力，遂給以境內閒田。

translations.literal: He also argued that the archers were all local men, skilled in frontier passes and paths, knowing Qiang speech and enduring frontier hardship, yet the state had never supplied them with weapons or provisions and in every battle made them face the enemy first — fearing there was no way to demand their utmost loyalty, he therefore granted them idle land within the district.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the archers were all local men, skilled in frontier passes and paths, knowing Qiang speech and enduring frontier hardship, yet the state had never supplied them with weapons or provisions and in every battle made them face the enemy first — fearing there was no way to demand their utmost loyalty, he therefore granted them idle land within the district.

sentences.zh: 春秋耕斂，州為出兵護作，而蠲其租。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn they plowed and harvested; the prefecture sent troops to protect the work and remitted their rent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn they plowed and harvested; the prefecture sent troops to protect the work and remitted their rent.

sentences.zh: 繼遷死，其子德明請命於朝。

translations.literal: When Jiqian died his son Deming requested appointment from the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian died his son Deming requested appointment from the court.

sentences.zh: 瑋言：「繼遷擅河南地二十年，兵不解甲，使中國有西顧之憂。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Jiqian held the lands south of the river for twenty years without laying down arms, causing China constant worry over the west."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Jiqian held the lands south of the river for twenty years without laying down arms, causing China constant worry over the west."

sentences.zh: 今國危子弱，不即捕滅，後更強盛，不可制。

translations.literal: "Now the state is in peril and the son is weak; if he is not captured and destroyed at once, when he grows stronger later he cannot be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the state is in peril and the son is weak; if he is not captured and destroyed at once, when he grows stronger later he cannot be controlled."

sentences.zh: 願假臣精兵，出其不意，禽德明送闕下，復河西為郡縣，此其時也。

translations.literal: "Your servant asks for elite troops to strike by surprise, seize Deming and send him to court, and restore Hexi as commanderies and counties — now is the time."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant asks for elite troops to strike by surprise, seize Deming and send him to court, and restore Hexi as commanderies and counties — now is the time."

sentences.zh: 」帝方以恩致德明，不報。

translations.literal: The emperor was then seeking to win Deming by kindness and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then seeking to win Deming by kindness and gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 既而西延家、妙俄、熟魏數大族請拔帳自歸，諸將猶豫不敢應。

translations.literal: Soon the Xiyanjia, Miao'e, Shuei, and several other great tribes asked to move their camps and submit; the generals hesitated and dared not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Xiyanjia, Miao'e, Shuei, and several other great tribes asked to move their camps and submit; the generals hesitated and dared not respond.

sentences.zh: 瑋曰：「德明野心，不急折其翮，後必颺去。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Deming has a wild heart; if his wings are not broken quickly, later he will surely fly away."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Deming has a wild heart; if his wings are not broken quickly, later he will surely fly away."

sentences.zh: 」即日，將其士薄大都山，受降者內徙，德明不敢拒。

translations.literal: That same day he led his soldiers close to Dadu Mountain; those who surrendered were moved inward, and Deming dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he led his soldiers close to Dadu Mountain; those who surrendered were moved inward, and Deming dared not resist.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閣門使，為環慶路兵馬都鈐轄，兼知邠州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Upper West Gate Commissioner, made Overall Controller of the Huanqing circuit's forces, and concurrently governor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Upper West Gate Commissioner, made Overall Controller of the Huanqing circuit's forces, and concurrently governor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，進東上閣門使。

translations.literal: When Mount Tai was enfeoffed he was promoted to Upper East Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Mount Tai was enfeoffed he was promoted to Upper East Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝以瑋習知河北事，乃以為真定路都鈐轄，領高州刺史。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Wei was familiar with Hebei affairs, he was made Overall Controller of the Zhending circuit and given charge of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor knew Wei was familiar with Hebei affairs, he was made Overall Controller of the Zhending circuit and given charge of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 瑋嘗上涇原、環慶兩道圖。

translations.literal: Wei had once submitted maps of the Jingyuan and Huanqing circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had once submitted maps of the Jingyuan and Huanqing circuits.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝以示左右，曰：「華夷山川城郭險固出入戰守之要，舉在是矣。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor showed them to those beside him and said: "The essentials of Chinese and barbarian mountains and rivers, walled cities, strong points, routes of advance and retreat, and points of attack and defense are all here."
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor showed them to those beside him and said, "The essentials of Chinese and barbarian mountains and rivers, walled cities, strong points, routes of advance and retreat, and points of attack and defense are all here."

sentences.zh: 」因敕別繪二圖，以一留樞密院，一付本道，俾諸將得按圖計事。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered two copies to be drawn separately, one kept in the Bureau of Military Affairs and one sent to the circuit, so that the generals could plan affairs according to the maps.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered two copies to be drawn separately, one kept in the Bureau of Military Affairs and one sent to the circuit, so that the generals could plan affairs according to the maps.

sentences.zh: 復為涇原路都鈐轄兼知渭州，與秦翰破章埋族于武延川，分兵滅撥臧於平涼，於是隴山諸族皆來獻地。

translations.literal: He was again made Overall Controller of the Jingyuan circuit and concurrently governor of Weizhou; with Qin Han he defeated the Zhangmai tribe at Wuyan River, divided his forces and destroyed Bozang at Pingliang, and thereupon all the tribes of Longshan came to offer their lands.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Overall Controller of the Jingyuan circuit and concurrently governor of Weizhou; with Qin Han he defeated the Zhangmai tribe at Wuyan River, divided his forces and destroyed Bozang at Pingliang, and thereupon all the tribes of Longshan came to offer their lands.

sentences.zh: 瑋築堡山外，為籠竿城，募士兵守之。

translations.literal: Wei built a fort outside Baoshan, made Longgan City, and recruited local soldiers to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built a fort outside Baoshan, established Longgan City, and recruited local soldiers to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 曰：「異時秦、渭有警，此必爭之地也。

translations.literal: He said: "If Qin and Wei should ever be alarmed, this will surely be contested ground."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If Qin and Wei should ever be alarmed, this will surely be contested ground."

sentences.zh: 」祀汾陰，進四方館使。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were performed at Fenyin he was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifices were performed at Fenyin he was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上表還州事，願專督軍旅。

translations.literal: After more than a year he submitted a memorial returning prefectural affairs and asking to devote himself solely to commanding the army.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he submitted a memorial returning prefectural affairs and asking to devote himself solely to commanding the army.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲遽更守臣，以密詔敦諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to change the frontier governor hastily and used a secret edict to urge him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to change the frontier governor hastily and used a secret edict to urge him earnestly.

sentences.zh: 改引進使、英州團練使，復知秦州，兼涇、原儀、渭、鎮戎緣邊安撫使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys and regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, again made governor of Qinzhou, and concurrently Frontier Pacification Commissioner for Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, and Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Commissioner for Introducing Envoys and regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, again made governor of Qinzhou, and concurrently Frontier Pacification Commissioner for Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, and Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 時唃廝嵒強盛，立遵佐之。

translations.literal: At that time Gusiluo was powerful and Lizun assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gusiluo was powerful and Lizun assisted him.

sentences.zh: 立遵乃上書求號「贊普」，瑋言：「贊普，可汗號也。

translations.literal: Lizun then submitted a memorial requesting the title "Zanpu"; Wei said: "Zanpu is a khan's title."
translations.idiomatic: Lizun then submitted a memorial requesting the title "Zanpu"; Wei said, "Zanpu is a khan's title."

sentences.zh: 立遵一言得之，何以處唃廝嵒邪？

translations.literal: "If Lizun obtains it with a single request, how are we to treat Gusiluo?"
translations.idiomatic: "If Lizun obtains it with a single request, how are we to treat Gusiluo?"

sentences.zh: 且復有求，漸不可制。

translations.literal: "Moreover, if he asks again, gradually he cannot be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, if he asks again, gradually he cannot be controlled."

sentences.zh: 」乃以立遵為保順軍節度使，恩如廝鐸督。

translations.literal: Lizun was therefore made military governor of the Baoshun Army, with favor like that shown to Siduodu.
translations.idiomatic: Lizun was therefore made military governor of the Baoshun Army, with favor like that shown to Siduodu.

sentences.zh: 西羌將舉事，必先定約束，號為「立文法」。

translations.literal: When the western Qiang were about to act they always first fixed regulations, called "establishing the law code."
translations.idiomatic: When the western Qiang were about to act they always first fixed regulations, called "establishing the law code."

sentences.zh: 唃廝嵒使其舅賞樣丹與廝敦立文法於離王族，謀內寇。

translations.literal: Gusiluo had his maternal uncle Shangyangdan and Sidun establish the law code among the Li royal clan and plotted invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo had his maternal uncle Shangyangdan and Sidun establish the law code among the Li royal clan and plotted invasion.

sentences.zh: 瑋陰結廝敦，解寶帶予之。

translations.literal: Wei secretly allied with Sidun and gave him a jeweled belt.
translations.idiomatic: Wei secretly allied with Sidun and gave him a jeweled belt.

sentences.zh: 廝敦感激，求自效，間謂瑋曰：「吾父何所使？

translations.literal: Sidun was deeply moved and offered his service; he privately said to Wei: "What does my father want of me?"
translations.idiomatic: Sidun was deeply moved and offered his service; he privately said to Wei, "What does my father want of me?"

sentences.zh: 欲吾首，猶可斷以獻。

translations.literal: "If he wants my head, I can still cut it off and present it."
translations.idiomatic: "If he wants my head, I can still cut it off and present it."

sentences.zh: 」瑋曰：「我知賞樣丹時至汝帳下，汝能為我取賞樣丹首乎？

translations.literal: Wei said: "I know Shangyangdan sometimes comes to your camp — can you get Shangyangdan's head for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "I know Shangyangdan sometimes comes to your camp — can you get Shangyangdan's head for me?"

sentences.zh: 」廝敦愕然應之。

translations.literal: Sidun, startled, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Sidun, startled, agreed.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，果斷其首來。

translations.literal: After more than ten days he indeed brought the severed head.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days he indeed brought the severed head.

sentences.zh: 廝敦因獻南市地。

translations.literal: Sidun thereupon offered the lands of Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sidun thereupon offered the lands of Nanshi.

sentences.zh: 南市者，秦、渭之阨也，瑋城之，表廝敦為順州刺史。

translations.literal: Nanshi was the choke point of Qin and Wei; Wei fortified it and recommended Sidun as Prefect of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanshi was the choke point of Qin and Wei; Wei fortified it and recommended Sidun as Prefect of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，張佶知秦州，置四門砦，侵奪羌地，羌人多叛去，畏得罪不敢出。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Jie governed Qinzhou, he set up the Four Gates fort and seized Qiang lands; many Qiang rebelled and fled, fearing punishment and not daring to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Jie governed Qinzhou, he set up the Four Gates fort and seized Qiang lands; many Qiang rebelled and fled, fearing punishment and not daring to come out.

sentences.zh: 瑋招出之，令入馬贖罪，還故地，至者數千人，每送馬六十匹，給彩一端。

translations.literal: Wei summoned them out, had them present horses to redeem their guilt, and restored their old lands; several thousand came, and for every sixty horses presented he gave one bolt of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Wei summoned them out, had them present horses to redeem their guilt, and restored their old lands; several thousand came, and for every sixty horses presented he gave one bolt of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 築弓門、冶坊、床穰、靜戎、三陽、定西、伏羌、永寧、小洛門、威遠十砦，浚壕三百八十里，皆役屬羌廂兵，工費不出民。

translations.literal: He built ten forts — Gongmen, Yefang, Chuangrang, Jingrong, Sanyang, Dingxi, Fuqiang, Yongning, Xiaoluomen, and Weiyuan — and dug trenches for three hundred eighty li, all using Qiang garrison troops, with labor costs not taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: He built ten forts — Gongmen, Yefang, Chuangrang, Jingrong, Sanyang, Dingxi, Fuqiang, Yongning, Xiaoluomen, and Weiyuan — and dug trenches for three hundred eighty li, all using Qiang garrison troops, with labor costs not taken from the people.

sentences.zh: 伏羌首領廝雞波、李磨論私立文法，瑋潛兵滅其帳。

translations.literal: The Fuqiang chiefs Sijibo and Limolun privately established the law code; Wei sent troops in secret and destroyed their camps.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuqiang chiefs Sijibo and Limolun privately established the law code; Wei sent troops in secret and destroyed their camps.

sentences.zh: 其年，唃廝嵒率眾數萬大入寇，瑋迎戰三都谷，追奔三十里，斬首千餘級，獲馬牛、雜畜、器仗三萬餘。

translations.literal: That year Gusiluo led tens of thousands in a major invasion; Wei met him at Sandu Valley, pursued the fleeing enemy thirty li, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured more than thirty thousand horses, cattle, miscellaneous livestock, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gusiluo led tens of thousands in a major invasion; Wei met him at Sandu Valley, pursued the fleeing enemy thirty li, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured more than thirty thousand horses, cattle, miscellaneous livestock, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 遷客省使、康州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Receptions and Defense Commissioner of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Receptions and Defense Commissioner of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 馬波叱臈立柵野吳谷，瑋選募神武軍二百人，斬柵，獲生口、孳畜甚眾。

translations.literal: Mapochila set palisades at Yewu Valley; Wei selected and recruited two hundred men of the Divine Martial Guard, cut down the palisades, and captured many prisoners and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Mapochila set palisades at Yewu Valley; Wei selected and recruited two hundred men of the Divine Martial Guard, cut down the palisades, and captured many prisoners and livestock.

sentences.zh: 宗哥大首領甘遵治兵于任奴川，瑋遣間殺遵，及破魚角蟬所立文法于吹麻城。

translations.literal: Ganzun, a great chief of Zongge, assembled troops at Rennu River; Wei sent agents to kill Ganzun and also broke the law code established by Yujiaocan at Chuima City.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzun, a great chief of Zongge, assembled troops at Rennu River; Wei sent agents to kill Ganzun and also broke the law code established by Yujiaocan at Chuima City.

sentences.zh: 既而河州、洮蘭、安江、妙敦、邈川、党逋諸城皆納質為熟戶。

translations.literal: Soon the cities of Hezhou, Taolan, Anjiang, Miaodun, Miaochuan, and Dangbu all sent hostages and became settled households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the cities of Hezhou, Taolan, Anjiang, Miaodun, Miaochuan, and Dangbu all sent hostages and became settled households.

sentences.zh: 時瑋作塹抵拶嵒嚨。

translations.literal: At that time Wei was building trenches against Zaziyan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei was building trenches against Zaziyan.

sentences.zh: 拶嵒嚨，西蕃要害地也。

translations.literal: Zaziyan was a key point of the western barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Zaziyan was a key point of the western barbarians.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑋遣小吏楊知進護賜物通甘州可汗王，還過宗哥界，立遵邀知進，語曰：「秦州大人直以兵入拶嵒嚨來，幸為我言，願罷兵，歲入貢，約蕃漢為一家。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei had sent the clerk Yang Zhijin to escort gifts to the Khan-King of Ganzhou; returning through Zongge territory, Lizun intercepted Zhijin and said: "The great man of Qinzhou is coming straight with troops into Zaziyan — please speak for me: I wish to cease hostilities, pay tribute yearly, and make barbarians and Chinese one family."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei had sent the clerk Yang Zhijin to escort gifts to the Khan-King of Ganzhou; returning through Zongge territory, Lizun intercepted Zhijin and said, "The great man of Qinzhou is coming straight with troops into Zaziyan — please speak for me: I wish to cease hostilities, pay tribute yearly, and make barbarians and Chinese one family."

sentences.zh: 」因使種人党失畢陵從知進來獻馬。

translations.literal: He therefore had the tribesman Dangshibiling follow Zhijin to come and present horses.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had the tribesman Dangshibiling follow Zhijin to come and present horses.

sentences.zh: 自是唃廝嵒勢蹙，退保磧中不出。

translations.literal: From then on Gusiluo's power was constricted; he withdrew to hold the desert interior and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Gusiluo's power was constricted; he withdrew to hold the desert interior and did not come out.

sentences.zh: 秦人請刻石紀功，有詔褒之。

translations.literal: The people of Qin requested a stone inscription to record the merit; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin requested a stone inscription to record the merit; an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，德明寇柔遠砦，都巡檢楊承吉與戰不利。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi, Deming raided Rouyuan Fort; the Overall Inspector Yang Chengji fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianxi, Deming raided Rouyuan Fort; the Overall Inspector Yang Chengji fought without success.

sentences.zh: 以瑋為華州觀察使、鄜延路副都總管、環、慶、秦等州緣邊巡檢安撫使。
